item.title: Dispatch Core [ALPHA]
item.description:
Your lines leave on time: timetables or intervals at the termini, measured
statistics for your whole network, a shared pool of reserve vehicles, and
since 0.20 station-to-station transfers with insertion into any line, at
the next timetable slot.

[b]What the mod does[/b]

[b]Measured statistics[/b] — The mod watches your vehicles and computes,
for every line: trip time, real frequency, average stop time, load and
speed. Nothing to configure, everything is measured as you play, and the
measurements survive saving.

[b]Timetables at the termini[/b] — Pick a line, switch it to Timetable
mode, add the departures of each hour (for example h03 and h33): your
vehicles will leave the termini at those minutes. Three settings frame the
rule: minimum stop (floor), delay tolerance, and maximum hold (a safety
ceiling so no vehicle ever waits forever). The "Single train on the line"
option silences false slot alerts when a lone vehicle alternates between
both termini, and manages itself when a second train joins or leaves.

[b]Interval mode (new in 0.21)[/b] — The other way to regulate, for ALL
transport modes: bus, tram, train, ship, plane. Two measures, your
choice: [b]in time[/b] (departures at each terminus are spaced exactly
the chosen duration apart, and the safety ceiling aligns itself with it)
or [b]in stops[/b] (a vehicle leaves only when the one ahead is at least
N stops away — the natural anti-bunching for urban lines). Between the
termini vehicles drive normally: only the wait at the terminus spaces
them.

[b]Reserve pool (trains)[/b] — Park a vehicle at any siding station from
its window: the parking line is created automatically, the vehicle drives
there on its own with closed doors, takes the first free track and turns
around to present its doors to the platform. When a slot is endangered for
lack of stock, a window proposes the available vehicles with distance and
estimated arrival. Pick one, it heads straight to the threatened terminus.
The reserve is shared network-wide: any parked vehicle can rescue any
compatible line.

[b]Transfer and assign (new in 0.20)[/b] — Send a parked vehicle to
another station, on the platform YOU pick (honored on arrival). Once at
the platform, "Assign to a line" lists every line serving that station:
the vehicle joins in place, loads passengers, and leaves at the next
displayed timetable slot. Reinforcing a line takes two clicks — and your
orders always override the wait.

[b]Built-in help[/b] — Dispatch menu > Help: short recipes to get
started, including the new Transfer / Assign section.

[b]What the mod does NOT do[/b]

[list]
[*] It NEVER touches your tracks, stations or lines: its only levers are
holding vehicles at platforms and its own technical lines, created and
cleaned up automatically.
[*] It never parks anything on its own: you decide, it executes.
[*] It does not replace the game's management: buying, selling and sending
to depots remain yours.
[*] Combined behaviour with other scheduling mods (e.g. Timetables) is
undefined: use only one regulation mod at a time.
[/list]

[b]Good to know[/b]

[list]
[*] A track-only station mod is required for clean sidings (see required
items).
[*] On a regulated line, set the GAME's minimum waiting time to zero at
the termini and use the mod's "Minimum stop" instead: the two settings
add up otherwise. The mod warns you in the log.
[*] Very long lines (round trip approaching one in-game hour) cannot be
regulated by timetable: the mod tells you.
[*] Never delete the "[Do not delete] Dispatch" lines yourself: the mod
takes care of them.
[*] Removing the mod mid-game leaves held vehicles behind: recall your
reserves first.
[/list]

[b]ALPHA version[/b] — The mod is functional and tested on large games,
and it evolves quickly. Feedback in the comments is welcome, especially
unexpected behaviour.

Interface and help translated into English, French and German.
